newsitem.title: USA: Parallel Petroleum reserves rose in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Parallel Petroleum reserves rose in 1996.

text.p: Parallel Petroleum Corp said Thursday its natural gas reserves increased by 25 percent during 1996 to 33 billion cubic feet from 26 billion a year ago, while proved oil reserves increased by 9 percent to 1.64 million barrels from 1.50 million a year ago.

Expressed in natural gas equivalents, with oil converted to natural gas on the basis of one barrel to 6,000 cubic feet, the reserves increased by 21 percent to 42.4 billion cubic feet equivalent from 35.1 billion, the company said.

It said this, along with price increases over the past year increased the discounted present value of the reserves by 159 percent to $67 million at year end from $26 million a year earlier based on Securities and Exchange guidelines, using a 10 percent discount rate and no escalation of production costs or product prices.

On an undiscounted basis, Parallel said, the future net cash flow of the reserves was estimated at $111 million versus $47 million a year ago, based on product prices and costs in effect at year-end 1996 and held constant for the life of the properties.
